title: Marguerite and the Cipher
premise: When retired detective Isandro Sterling discovers that the diary of Marguerite Vale—a woman who vanished twenty years ago—contains entries written after her disappearance, he realizes she may still be alive, hidden in plain sight. Following the diary's ciphered marginalia through the town's buried history, he uncovers a conspiracy of silence involving the families who profited from her disappearance and the witness everyone swore was dead: Marguerite herself, living under another name. As the conspirators close in to destroy the diary and its keeper, Isandro must choose between protecting the town's fragile peace and giving Marguerite her stolen life back. In the end, he exposes the truth at great personal cost—the bookshop burns, his oldest friendship shatters—but Marguerite finally steps into the light, and Isandro finds the belonging he never had in Hollow Creek.
about_author: Emrys Blackwood is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed court records before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about quiet places where the past refuses to stay filed.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Absence
chapters.summary: Isandro Sterling, POV. In his failing bookshop, Isandro alphabetizes a donated box of books and finds Marguerite Vale's diary tucked inside a hollowed-out atlas. The final entry is dated three weeks after her disappearance. Emotional beat: unease—the orderly life he built begins to tilt.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. He rereads the diary overnight, recognizing his own younger handwriting in the margins—he was the investigating detective. Flashbacks establish the case that ended his career. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a bruise he'd learned to ignore.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. He visits the riverbank where the search ended and meets Tamsin Cole, a young journalist digging into the anniversary of the disappearance. She notices the diary's coded marginalia. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two lonely people circling the same wound.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Isandro and Tamsin, alternating POV. Working in the shop after hours, they crack the first layer: a book-based cipher keyed to titles on his own shelves—someone chose him deliberately. Emotional beat: dawning wonder curdling into fear; this was left for him.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek's Benefactors
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. The decoded entries name three founding families whose fortunes rose the year Marguerite vanished. At a town gala, Isandro watches Aldous Merrick, patriarch of the richest family, watch him back. Emotional beat: the town's warmth revealed as surveillance.

chapters.title: An Entry After the End
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV (first time). A present-day diary entry: a woman called 'Ruth' living quietly, writing in code because she cannot stop writing. She knows someone found the atlas. Emotional beat: terror braided with longing—she wants to be found and cannot afford to be.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. He tracks down the retired coroner who signed Marguerite's death certificate without a body. The old man, frightened, admits he was paid—and that night his house is ransacked. Emotional beat: the cost of old sins coming due.

chapters.title: Smoke in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. An 'accidental' fire damages the bookshop's back room—the section holding the atlas and his case files. Tamsin pulls him out. Emotional beat: rage and grief; they've escalated from watching to burning.

chapters.title: Ruth
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. 'Ruth' tends bees outside town, invisible for twenty years, sustained by routine and the diary as her only true self. She learns of the fire and knows what it means. Emotional beat: the price of survival itemized—every year bought with silence.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Isandro and Tamsin, POV. The burned fragments reveal a second cipher layer pointing to the defunct mill where Marguerite worked. There Isandro finds a child's shoe and a hidden room—evidence of something worse than murder. Emotional beat: dread deepening; the crime has roots.

chapters.title: Aldous Merrick Invites You to Dinner
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Merrick hosts Isandro for an elegant, menacing dinner, offering to save the bookshop if the diary 'goes away.' He speaks of Marguerite in the past tense, convincingly. Emotional beat: temptation and loathing; the price of survival offered to Isandro too.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Story
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Her editor kills her investigation under pressure from the paper's owner—a Merrick cousin. She publishes online anyway, alone. Emotional beat: defiance and isolation; belonging means risking everything you have.

chapters.title: The Child Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Flashback interleaved with present: the hidden room held not a victim but her hiding place—she fled to protect her infant son, given away the night she disappeared. Emotional beat: heartbreak; memory as both refuge and prison.

chapters.title: Following Bees
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Deciphering a reference to 'hives by the water,' Isandro finds Ruth's cottage. Through the window he sees her face—older, alive, unmistakably Marguerite. Emotional beat: awe and tenderness; twenty years collapse in a single glance.

chapters.title: Two Detectives, One Truth
chapters.summary: Isandro and Marguerite, alternating POV. In the cottage they finally speak: why she ran, what the Merricks did, why the diary had to continue past her death—to prove she lived. Emotional beat: catharsis; being believed after decades of erasure.

chapters.title: The Son
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. The adopted son, now a deputy sheriff named Caleb Vale, is Merrick's protégé. Isandro must decide whether telling him will arm an ally or alert the enemy. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; truth as a weapon that cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Caleb Reads the Diary
chapters.summary: Caleb, POV. Given the diary, Caleb reads his mother's handwriting describing the day she gave him up. Shattered, he chooses her over Merrick and brings the department's sealed evidence. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; belonging reclaimed across time.

chapters.title: The Mill at Midnight
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The group meets at the mill to photograph evidence, but Merrick's men are waiting. A standoff; Tamsin livestreams it as leverage. Emotional beat: white-knuckle tension; the past physically closing in.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. The mill catches fire during the confrontation. Isandro goes back in for the evidence and nearly dies; Merrick, trying to burn it all, is caught fleeing by Caleb. Emotional beat: sacrifice; the price of survival paid in full, willingly.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. In the courthouse, Marguerite testifies—her voice steady, her name spoken aloud in public for the first time in twenty years. The town listens. Emotional beat: vindication and vulnerability; memory finally honored instead of buried.

chapters.title: Ashes and Inventory
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. The bookshop is gone, but the community that once watched him now rebuilds it, shelf by shelf. He and Tamsin sort salvaged books; among them, the scorched atlas. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal; ruin making room for belonging.

chapters.title: Marguerite and the Cipher
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Isandro, shared POV. Spring: Marguerite signs her real name on the shop's new ledger; Caleb visits weekly; the diary gets one last entry, dated today, in plain unencoded words. Emotional beat: peace earned—the cipher solved, the woman found, the man no longer filing secrets but living openly among them.
